rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Page geometry dies at the cut; reading order survives.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 4 "Start here": raw line 22: "the lecture below hands you the lenses to read it with." At pin ba5ccf5 this was spatially true: the two lecture include-links ('[Lecture: Reading the return]', '[Lecture: Learning through contrast]') sat in the SAME `##` chunk, no heading between them (verified via `git show ba5ccf5:.../learn-from-the-test.md`). This diff inserted new chunk 5 ('## Say what done-done means', raw lines 26-38) between the blockquote that closes chunk 4 and those two links, so the links now render on a DIFFERENT slide, one chunk later, with an entire unrelated section in between. Harm: on the composed 'Start here' slide a reader (solo student or trainer) is told a lecture is coming up next; the very next slide is not the lecture at all but 'Say what done-done means', an unrelated prompt-and-explain beat -- the promise fails at the moment of turning the page, and the eventual lecture links only surface at the tail end of that intervening slide with nothing tying them back to the earlier claim. This is the rule's own canonical failure shape (prework's 'the repo itself (picked in Step 1 below)' stranded slides ahead of Step 1). Not covered by any maintainer accept-note: the file's one 'Slide deixis accepted' note (raw line 149) names a different phrase ('the bullets back', a verb phrase, unrelated); the 'Done-done opener' note (raw line 124) documents the new section's placement and pedagogy rationale but never addresses this side effect on the preceding slide's claim. Mechanical gate `node scripts/check-slide-deixis.js --file <this file> --report` returns clean, but only because its geometry-object word list (read directly from `scripts/check-slide-deixis.js`'s OBJ regex) omits 'lecture' -- a genuine tool vocabulary gap, not a clearance.
